title: The Broken Cup That Grew a Garden

shots.caption: IT LEAKED BEFORE THE FIRST SIP.
SHE GAVE THE CUP A NEW JOB.
THE CRACK LET THE WATER THROUGH.
SHE CAME BACK IN THE RAIN.
THEY MADE ROOM FOR EVERY SEED.
THE CUP HAD NOT BEEN USELESS.
IT HAD BECOME A PLACE TO GROW.
SOME THINGS BLOOM THROUGH THE CRACKS.

creative_intent.logline: A stick-figure woman cannot stop a cracked cup from leaking, so she gives it a new purpose as a planter; one small sprout inspires a shared garden of imperfect vessels.
creative_intent.hook: A cup leaks its water before the first sip; the figure tries to patch it while every drop escapes.
creative_intent.theme: A thing does not need to return to its old shape to become useful again.
creative_intent.emotional_turn: The cracked cup that could not hold water becomes the first pot in a community garden.
creative_intent.character_bible: Lead: white round-headed 2D stick figure with articulated limbs, expressive face and a persistent yellow wristband. Helper: same visual construction and scale family, distinguished by a blue scarf. No realistic humans, anime, or character redesign between shots.
creative_intent.prop_bible: One pale ceramic cup with a visible zig-zag crack; soil, a single seed, then a sprout and flower. The same cup remains identifiable as it changes function. During the wind beat it visibly tips onto its side; planting and watering use crouched two-hand contact poses.
narrative_beats: 0–30s: cup leaks immediately; lead tries to patch the crack; visual hook and failure.
30–60s: the cup is discarded; a seed rolls into frame and changes the lead's attention.
60–90s: lead repurposes the cup as a planter; wind knocks it down; she tries again.
90–120s: a stranger with a blue scarf offers soil; both plant and water the seed.
120–150s: no immediate result; lead returns through rain; a green tip appears.
150–180s: others bring broken cups; a tiny shared garden forms.
180–210s: first flower opens; lead offers it to the helper; the original crack remains visible.

concept_selection.scoring_scale: 0-100 weighted editorial assessment; not measured audience performance

candidates.name: The Broken Cup That Grew a Garden
candidates.reason: One instantly legible leaking prop evolves into a flower and a shared garden; action-led and technically achievable with the existing 2D puppet rig.

candidates.name: The Last Light on the Block
candidates.reason: A lone figure relights street lamps for strangers, then discovers the final lamp illuminates their own dark window.

candidates.name: The Quiet Apology
candidates.reason: A paper note passes between two estranged figures through visible actions, ending with a repaired shared object.

concept_selection.selected: The Broken Cup That Grew a Garden

thumbnail_concepts: A giant cracked white cup leaks blue water while a tiny yellow-wristband stick figure reaches for it; dark navy background and one bright green sprout.
A split transformation: empty cracked cup on the left, flower-filled cup garden on the right, the two stick figures meeting in the middle.
Close-up of a blue-scarf helper and yellow-wristband lead placing soil into the cracked cup as the first flower opens behind them.
title_alternatives: The Broken Cup That Grew a Garden
She Couldn’t Fix the Cup—So She Gave It a New Purpose
A Cracked Cup, One Seed, and a New Beginning
creative_intent.description_angle: A silent 2D stick-figure short film about changing purpose instead of giving up on something imperfect. Told through physical action, with original instrumental music and no voiceover.
growth_hypotheses: The immediate leak in the first five seconds may make the conflict understandable without dialogue; validate using audience retention at 0:05.
The cup-to-flower transformation may improve completion and rewatch; validate against average percentage viewed and retention dips.
The two-character garden payoff may invite sharing; validate with shares per view and qualitative comments.

sources.finding: YouTube reports 6.5B microdrama views in H1 2026 and over 70% year-over-year growth in APAC-related views; evidence supports concise emotional serial storytelling, not a guarantee for this 16:9 film.
Third-party weekly tracker shows stickman animation demand at 2.93M on-topic views/day for week 2026-11-06, down 18% versus 30 days earlier; category is crowded and broad demand is soft.
Third-party weekly tracker shows inspiring animated films at 386K on-topic views/day, down 12% versus 28 days earlier; a distinct visual metaphor is preferable to a generic motivational message.

trend_research.conclusion: Do not chase generic stickman volume. Use a specific visual metaphor, a fast emotional hook, and a satisfying object transformation.

audio_plan.music: Original procedural instrumental in five emotional phases: leak/tension, failed repair, discovery, collaboration, bloom/payoff.
audio_plan.sfx: Procedurally synthesized ceramic taps, timed water drops, seed movement, soil taps and rain hiss, generated from each shot cue; no third-party samples or existing songs.
